gqm.goal: Prevent documented implementation workflows from omitting verification of their runnable examples.
questions: Does the workflow require a documented example to be exercised?

analysis_skills.name: requirements-review
analysis_skills.evidence: The change has concrete acceptance requirements: a documented example must be executed, route decisions must be explicit, and final evidence must be specific.

analysis_skills.name: architecture-review
analysis_skills.evidence: The change remains within implementation-orchestrator and its internal components; it adds no dependency or responsibility boundary.

analysis_skills.name: change-impact-review
analysis_skills.evidence: Consumers are agents using implementation plans, acceptance contracts, and final evidence; the changed template and components are their only direct impact surface.

analysis_skills.name: security-review
analysis_skills.evidence: No trust boundary, input parser, secret handling, or external command behavior was added; make lint runs gitleaks as a deterministic control.

analysis_skills.name: whitebox-risk-based-test
analysis_skills.evidence: The focused test protects the added guidance against deletion; the full pytest suite covers validator and installer regressions.

must_quality.rule: Requested behavior is satisfied and demonstrated by tests or evidence
Existing supported behavior is not unintentionally broken
Repository-local guidance and public contracts are respected
No critical security defect is introduced

performance_quality.rule: Keep responsibilities, names, and tests easy to evolve

critical_defects: Data loss, corruption, or unsafe migration
Required behavior missing or public API broken without approval
assumptions: The repository has Python validator tests and Makefile formatting, lint, and secret-scan commands; it has no build artifact or deployment workflow.
